title: Choosing the right JOIN for the job

items.stem: A school wants a report that lists every student with the course they are enrolled in, and students with no enrollment must still appear with a blank course. Every enrollment row refers to a real student. Which query fits?

options.text: students INNER JOIN enrollments, matching on student_id
students LEFT JOIN enrollments, matching on student_id
enrollments LEFT JOIN students, matching on student_id
students INNER JOIN enrollments, then drop blank courses

items.stem: A teacher wants to email only the students who are enrolled in at least one course, using the students and enrollments tables. Which join type should be used: INNER JOIN or LEFT JOIN? Answer with the join type only.
An advisor wants a list of students who have never enrolled in any course. The enrollments table has a non-NULL enrollment_id in every row. Which query returns exactly those students?

options.text: students INNER JOIN enrollments, keeping rows where enrollment_id IS NULL
students LEFT JOIN enrollments, keeping rows where enrollment_id IS NOT NULL
students LEFT JOIN enrollments, keeping rows where enrollment_id IS NULL
students INNER JOIN enrollments, keeping rows where student_id IS NOT NULL

items.stem: The students table has 4 students. Their enrollment rows are: Ana 3, Ben 1, Cy 0, Dee 2. A query runs students LEFT JOIN enrollments, matching on student_id, with no WHERE clause. How many rows does it return?

A report runs departments LEFT JOIN courses, grouped by department, and must show 0 for a department that has no courses. Which expression should be used for the count: COUNT(*) or COUNT(courses.course_id)? Answer with the expression.
A query is students LEFT JOIN enrollments ON students.student_id = enrollments.student_id WHERE enrollments.term = 'Fall'. What happens to a student who has no enrollments at all?

options.text: They are removed, because a NULL term fails the filter
They stay, with a NULL term in their row
They stay, because LEFT JOIN keeps all students
The query fails, because term can be NULL
